overall: Atlanta is having a morning defined by persistent overcast (OVC, 100% cloud cover, ceiling ~335m) that suppressed warming through the early hours, keeping temps stuck in the 71-74°F range from midnight through 10:52 ET. However, the past hour saw a sharp jump to 78.8°F (running max) with a strong positive velocity of +5.4°F/hr, suggesting the cloud deck is beginning to erode or break — consistent with the NWS 'mostly sunny' afternoon call. Humidity remains high with a 69.8°F dewpoint, and a slight storm chance arrives after 5 PM.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster in a relatively tight band: ECMWF 85.5°F, HRRR 83.9°F, NBM 86.2°F (consensus ~85.2°F), all running 2-3°F below the NWS point forecast of 88°F. The overcast morning likely caused observed temps to lag behind model expectations in early hours, but the recent rapid heating suggests afternoon clearing may push temps toward the NWP range. The META model (most reliable fused signal) strongly favors the 84-85°F bucket at 29.1%, with secondary probability in 86-87°F (20.5%) and 88-89°F (16.8%).
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 78.8°F at 11:52 ET and peak timing expected around 14:42–15:00 ET (~3 hours out), roughly 6-8°F of additional heating is needed to reach the NWP consensus of ~85°F. The current +5.4°F/hr velocity is likely a transient cloud-break burst rather than a sustained rate; a more realistic afternoon average of ~2°F/hr over 3 hours adds ~6°F, landing near 85°F. Confidence is moderate — the META model's 29.1% mass in the 84-85°F bucket is the strongest single signal, the ensemble flags a low-confidence, no-trade environment (Tier 4, high entropy), and afternoon storm initiation after 5 PM is unlikely to cap the daytime peak. Best estimate: 85-86°F, with meaningful tail risk toward 87-88°F if cloud clearing is more complete than current OVC conditions suggest.
